correctness.rationale: Each 0<h<2 kick–drift symplectic Euler S_h is elliptic with det 1, no invariant real line and unique invariant SPD metric P_h=[[1,h/2],[h/2,1]] up to scale. Cone Perron–Frobenius yields nonzero positive semidefinite right and left spectral-radius eigenmatrices, both forced positive definite by absence of real eigendirections. Strict equality in determinant-root Minkowski concavity for T(P)=E[S_HP S_H^T] would impose a common invariant P for almost all h, impossible for a nonpoint law; thus rho>1. A dual SPD eigenmatrix Q gives E[X_k^T Q X_k]=rho^k x0^TQx0, hence uniform two-sided Euclidean moment bounds. Exact symbolic recomputation gives jitter trace quotient 2 δ²(h²+δ²)/(4−h²), and the rational two-step matrix has characteristic polynomial (64z³−66z²+49z−49)/64. Random product finite-step enumeration only cross-checks, not proof.

value.rationale: The sharp all-nondegenerate-iid timesteps classification pinpoints an infinite-horizon mean-square instability invisible from stable deterministic steps and finite-horizon energy estimates. It includes an all-initial-state uniform rate, a two-point rational example whose mean contracts while second moments inflate, and quantitative small-jitter rate. These are useful structural reliability boundaries, not a routine simulation experiment.
